+### ADR-0040
 
+**Durable internal work handoff and the worker plane**
+
+- **Status:** Approved.
+- **Context:** [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md) runs background processing as its own deployment sharing the approved persistence and coordination contracts and makes no cloud message bus an MVP prerequisite, and [04](04-technology-stack-and-deployment.md) mandates no broker and names an optional maintenance worker in topology 2. ADR-0035 makes another scope's row read as missing and left the outbox to a later spec, ADR-0036 left worker leases and the purge of expired coordination rows across scopes to ISK-0009, ADR-0038 fixed two executables and left where maintenance work runs, and ADR-0039 left the worker's place in the developer topology.
+- **Decision:** A module enqueues a work item through `IWorkOutbox` in `Iskender.Domain.Ports`, in its own open unit of work, so the item commits or rolls back with the change that caused it, and an enqueue with the scope, kind, and idempotency key of a retained item writes nothing. Items are kept in PostgreSQL alone, in `isk_work`, with no broker, queue service, Kafka, `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY`, or cloud SDK, and a payload is at most 65,536 bytes and holds no secret, credential, prompt, or response text. Each item goes to one handler, at least once, with its database effects applied at most once and no ordering, broadcast, or publish/subscribe, and a handler makes its external effects idempotent itself. The dispatcher polls, takes a PostgreSQL-issued lease on one of a scope's shards, records each attempt before its handler runs, and applies the item in a unit of the item's own scope fenced by that lease, and a Redis or local lease coordinator refuses it with `MandatoryPath`. Failures are permanent, transient, unclassified, or abandoned, retried with jittered exponential backoff and poisoned at the attempt limit, and an unreachable database counts no attempt. Recurring jobs are defined in code with a name, interval, and batch, each run holding an operator-scope PostgreSQL lease, and ISK-0009 ships `coordination.purge_expired` and `work.retention`. Scopes with work are found only through a scope directory table kind in `isk_directory`, the one exception to ADR-0035's rule that another scope's row reads as missing: an operator-scope unit may read every directory row, which holds only the canonical scope, the module, and a due time, and each row becomes a unit scope only through `DirectoryScopeResolver`, a framework-internal ISK-0002 ownership resolver that rule H6 of the public contracts and versioning contract now allows, so no operator unit reads a tenant's item. The PostgreSQL coordinator registers a scope in the directory in the same unit as a write that creates an expiring row. The dispatcher and jobs run only in the worker, a third composition plane that the control-plane executable runs with its `work` command, with no new image or executable, its own root `AddIskenderWorker(...)` in `Iskender.Management`, `service.name` `iskender-worker`, the single-instance lease `instance.worker`, and only the health listener. The data plane and the serving control plane only enqueue. At the stop signal the worker claims nothing more and lets in-flight items finish within ADR-0038's stop bound. The developer topology gains a `worker` service with its own documents, which select PostgreSQL leases. Eight `work.*` error codes raise `core-contracts` to version 6, and events 8001 to 8012 are written under the category `Iskender.Work`. The current work contract, linked from the Persistence, publication and distributed coordination section of [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md) and first published by ISK-0009, holds the exact rules, with the persistence, coordination, hosting, container, and local environment contracts it revised.
+- **Rationale:** Writing the item in the caller's unit removes the window in which a crash between the change and the handoff loses work, and recording each attempt and fencing each apply keeps a crashed or stalled worker from applying an item twice. Finding work through a directory that names only scopes, and handling each item in its own scope's unit, keeps cross-tenant reads to the fact that a scope has work. A command of the existing control-plane executable scales and is secured apart from the serving planes without a new image.
+- **Consequences / trade-offs:** Delivery waits up to one poll interval plus backoff, and no latency figure is asserted. A crashing item stalls its shard until the shard's lease expires. The worker's leases must be PostgreSQL's, even where the planes take theirs from Redis. Every enqueue adds one or two statements, and every coordination write that creates an expiring row adds a directory insert. A handler or job runs only where it is registered, and the worker composes only the container contract's Entry points rule 2 registrations, so a later handler needs a revision of that contract. Finished items keep their payloads until `work.retention` deletes them, and that retention is also the idempotency window. The ports are in the embeddable `Iskender.Domain`, so the work contract's version, not the harness, is the commitment. Until ISK-0021, no process connects to PostgreSQL, so the worker dispatches nothing.
+- **References:** [03](03-domain-and-technical-architecture.md), [04](04-technology-stack-and-deployment.md), [05](05-identity-security-and-privacy.md), [08](08-routing-resilience-and-governance.md), [17](17-master-spec-inventory.md).
